- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement to prevent false bullishness.  
- If true outcome shows sharp spike followed by correction, model should not overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.  
- If history shows mean-reverting pattern (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending up then down), model should not assume continuation.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is flat, consider slight downward bias to account for lack of momentum.  
- If forecast is rising >5% from prior day and true outcome is falling, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% to avoid lagged overreaction.
